oewn-05101152-n.learner: a place on a scale of how strong, how much, or how good something is
examples: Here again I shall give you pain--to what degree you only can tell.
her realism is real to a degree which makes the false realism of our own day look merely dead-alive

oewn-13962925-n.learner: a particular point you can pick out in a range, in a series, or above all in a process
examples: she was preparing to see him with a degree of composure which astonished her husband and daughters
He was received by Mrs. Bennet with a degree of civility which made her two daughters ashamed

oewn-06710094-n.learner: an award given by a college or university to show that someone has finished a course of study well enough
examples: She earned a degree in history from the university.
He is studying for a degree in law.

oewn-08230738-n.learner: a part of an army smaller than a division, which can be split into several companies, squadrons, or batteries, and often into two battalions
examples: I cried for two days together when Colonel Miller's regiment went away.
They will then join his regiment, unless they are first invited to Longbourn

oewn-05991037-n.learner: a result you mean to bring about, or one that shapes what you plan to do
examples: "Is that his design in settling here?"
coming into Hertfordshire with the design of selecting a wife

oewn-05736623-n.learner: a way in which the parts of something are arranged
examples: The design of the new kitchen makes it easy to move around.
A poor design of the handle made the cup hard to hold.

oewn-00929892-n.learner: the work of deciding what form something will take, as by making a sketch, an outline, or a plan
examples: Design of the new engine took two years.
She works in the design of small boats.

oewn-00902866-v.learner: to bring one person to another so that they come to know each other in person
examples: Mrs. Long has promised to introduce him.
"Yes; he introduced us to his sister."

oewn-01621712-v.learner: to bring something into a new place or setting, or to set it up there
examples: Settlers introduced rabbits to the island.
The school introduced a rule about phones.

oewn-02082838-v.learner: to bring a new person or thing into a place that is already familiar
examples: They introduced a new pupil into the class halfway through the year.
He introduced a second cat into the quiet house.

oewn-13267561-n.learner: a large piece of land, especially in the country, that the owner keeps for their own use
examples: his father, who had intended to purchase an estate, but did not live to do it
"his estate there is a noble one"

oewn-13271829-n.learner: everything you own, both land and other things, together with everything you owe
examples: Her estate included her savings, her house, and her debts.
The lawyer drew up a list of the whole estate.

oewn-08184264-n.learner: one of the main social classes of a country, taken as a group forming part of the body of the nation, which in the past held political rights of its own
examples: The clergy were one of the three estates.
Each estate sent its own men to the assembly.

oewn-01970868-v.learner: to jump in a small, light way
examples: The sparrow hopped along the path.
The children hopped and skipped down the lane.

oewn-02099066-v.learner: to make a jump forward or upward
examples: He hopped up onto the low wall.
She hopped forward to reach the front of the line.

oewn-02099489-v.learner: to go quickly from one place to another
examples: She hopped over to her neighbour's house for a minute.
He hops between the office and the workshop all day.

oewn-13708765-n.learner: the main unit of money in Great Britain and Northern Ireland, worth 100 pence
examples: Mr. Bingley inherited property to the amount of nearly a hundred thousand pounds from his father
There was also a legacy of one thousand pounds.

oewn-13742201-n.learner: a unit of weight equal to sixteen ounces
examples: She bought a pound of butter at the market.
The fish weighed just over a pound.

oewn-04000061-n.learner: a public place with a fence where dogs that are lost or have no licence are kept
examples: The stray was taken to the pound.
We found our dog at the pound the next day.

oewn-02302103-v.learner: to put something before someone so that they can take it or turn it down
examples: Then, turning to Mr. Bennet, he offered himself as his antagonist at backgammon.
He offered me the last seat, but I said no.

oewn-02332196-v.learner: to give someone something useful, or something they need
examples: she walked here on Wednesday morning to condole with us, and offered her services
The neighbours offered us food and warm clothes.

oewn-02302909-v.learner: to make something available for people to have or use
examples: The hotel offers free parking to its guests.
The library offers a quiet room for study.

oewn-00592914-v.learner: to come to be aware of something
examples: If I can perceive her regard for him, he must be a simpleton indeed not to discover it too.
Elizabeth perceived that she must wait for her own visit there, to know the rest.

oewn-02110960-v.learner: to come to know that something is there by seeing, hearing, or feeling it
examples: I could perceive a light far off across the water.
She perceived a faint smell of smoke in the hall.

oewn-02510211-v.learner: to make someone do something through pressure or need, whether by bodily strength, by moral weight, or by argument
examples: Mr. Bingley was unaffectedly civil in his answer, and forced his younger sister to be civil also
Elizabeth was forced to give in to a little falsehood here

oewn-01653967-v.learner: to urge or drive a person to act; to hold them to it or give them a reason for it
examples: A strange curiosity forced him to open the letter.
Her sense of duty forced her to speak at last.

oewn-01519166-v.learner: to push someone or something into an action or state, or out of one, either in body or in a figure of speech
examples: Poverty forced the family from their home.
The rising water forced them onto the roof.
